page: Microsoft Azure D2a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DAv4 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The configuration includes 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The server includes 51 GB of local storage, while containing no GPUs and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2697.89. However, multi-core performance is weak, scoring 2697.89 (bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block cached bandwidth scoring in the bottom 10% at 128.19 GB/sec, and large block uncached write bandwidth at 24.14 GB/sec (bottom 25%). Geekbench testing shows average single-core performance (1522.0) but poor multi-core scaling (1952.0, bottom 10%), alongside poor results in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing.

This hardware profile represents an entry-level general-purpose tier where single-threaded tasks perform adequately, as evidenced by average single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, resource-intensive workloads face significant constraints. Database operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations all register in the bottom 10% of benchmarks. Consequently, this server is suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic utility scripting, or development environments rather than high-throughput database hosting, parallel processing, or large-scale web serving.
